'''Paul Jamaine Washington Jr.''' (born August 23, 1998<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Townsend |first=Brad |date=April 19, 2024 |title=How P.J. Washington, the hometown kid, helped spark Dallas Mavericks' late-season charge |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2024/04/19/how-pj-washington-the-hometown-kid-helped-spark-dallas-mavericks-late-season-charge/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419162117/https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2024/04/19/how-pj-washington-the-hometown-kid-helped-spark-dallas-mavericks-late-season-charge/|url-status=live |archive-date=April 19, 2024 |website=The Dallas Morning News}}</ref>) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]].

After being selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the 12th overall pick, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] in 2020. Washington was traded to the Mavericks at the trade deadline in February 2024, helping the team reach the [[2024 NBA Finals]].

==Early life==
Washington was born in [[Louisville, Kentucky]]. His family moved to [[St. Louis]] and [[Chicago]] before settling in [[Frisco, Texas|Frisco]], [[Texas]]. Washington attended [[Prime Prep Academy]] in [[Dallas]] after a brief stint at [[Lone Star High School]] in [[Frisco, Texas|Frisco]], before transferring to [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]], where he joined fellow five-star recruits [[Allonzo Trier]] and [[Derryck Thornton]].<ref name=":0" /> As junior, he averaged 16.8 points, 9.5 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game. After his junior season, Washington suited up for his [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team, Team Penny, sponsored by former NBA All-Star [[Penny Hardaway]], on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|Nike EYBL]] circuit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article88666737.html|title=Top power forward P.J. Washington has Kentucky roots, and UK wants him for 2017|last=Roberts|first=Ben|date=July 10, 2016|website=[[Lexington Herald Leader]]|access-date=May 4, 2024}}</ref> As a senior, Washington averaged 19.6 points, 9.4 rebounds and 6.1 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/nv/henderson/findlay-prep-pilot/athletes/pj-washington/basketball/stats/?careerid=4l68ic57ohivf|title=PJ Washington Findlay Prep Stats|website=MaxPreps.com|access-date=May 4, 2024}}</ref> Washington was selected to both the 2017 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/kentucky-signee-p-j-washington-blessed-to-continue-the-findlay-prep-tradition-at-the-jordan-brand-classic|title=Kentucky signee PJ Washington continues Findlay Prep tradition at Jordan Brand Classic|date=March 2, 2017|website=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=May 4, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aseaofblue.com/2017/1/15/14282264/4-kentucky-wildcats-named-to-mcdonalds-all-american-game|title=4 Kentucky Wildcats Named to McDonald's All-American Game|last=Marcum|first=Jason|date=January 15, 2017|website=A Sea of Blue|access-date=May 4, 2024}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Washington was rated as a five-star recruit and the No. 12 overall recruit and No. 3 power forward in the 2017 high school class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/PJ-Washington-38650|title=P.J. Washington, Findlay Prep, Power Forward|website=247sports.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/187810/pj-washington|title=P.J. Washington – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles|publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/p-j-washington-835|title=PJ Washington, 2017 Power forward – Rivals.com|website=n.rivals.com|access-date=November 6, 2017}}</ref> On November 10, 2016, he committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], signing his letter of intent on November 20.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/2017/08/11/pj-washington-kentucky-wildcats-recruiting|title=Versatile PJ Washington a key cog in Kentucky's Reloading Effort|last=Niesen|first=Joan|date=August 11, 2017|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|access-date=May 4, 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Throughout most of his freshman season at Kentucky, Washington played through a pinkie injury that required surgery in the summer. In the NCAA Tournament loss to [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], Washington led Kentucky with 18 points and 15 rebounds.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hale |first1=Jon |title=Can Reid Travis and PJ Washington play together in the same UK lineup? |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2018/08/08/kentucky-basketball-reid-travis-pj-washington-starting-lineups/911775002/ |access-date=August 9, 2018 |work=[[Louisville Courier-Journal]] |date=August 8, 2018}}</ref> Washington averaged 10.8 points and 5.7 rebounds per game as a freshman. After the season, he declared for the NBA draft, but announced his return on May 30, 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=PJ Washington will return as Kentucky's leading scorer; Wenyen Gabriel, Jarred Vanderbilt staying in draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23653768/pj-washington-returning-kentucky-wildcats-wenyen-gabriel-stay-nba-draft |access-date=August 9, 2018 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=May 30, 2018}}</ref>

Following Kentucky's loss to [[2018–19 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Washington announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]], where he was projected to be a first-round selection.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26477360/kentucky-washington-declares-nba-draft|title=Kentucky's Washington declares for NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 9, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Charlotte Hornets (2019–2024)===
Washington was selected as the 12th overall pick by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Quinton|last=Wash|title=Hornets Select PJ Washington With The 12th Pick In The 2019 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-select-pj-washington-12th-pick-2019-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=July 4, 2019}}</ref> On July 3, 2019, Washington officially signed with the Hornets<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign First-Round Draft Pick PJ Washington|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-sign-first-round-draft-pick-pj-washington|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2019|access-date=July 4, 2019}}</ref> and on October 23 he made his debut in NBA, started in a 126–125 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]] with 27 points, 4 rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block. He also made 7 three-pointers, the most in an NBA debut in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets rookie Washington nets 27 in 126–125 win over Bulls|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160625|website=ESPN.com|date=October 23, 2019|access-date=October 23, 2019}}</ref> On October 31, he scored 23 points and 8 rebounds in a 118–111 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets rally from 14 down to beat winless Kings 118–111|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160706|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=October 30, 2019|access-date=October 31, 2019}}</ref> On November 29, Washington put up 26 points and 5 rebounds in a 110–107 victory against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets edge Pistons again, 110–107|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160910|website=ESPN.com|date=November 29, 2019|access-date=November 29, 2019}}</ref> On September 15, 2020, Washington was named [[NBA All-Rookie Team|2019–20 NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] by the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ja Morant, Zion Williamsom headline 2019–20 Kia All-Rookie First Team Tyler Herro, Rui Hachimura voted to Second Team|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/09/15/nba-2019-20-all-rookie-first-team-official-release|website=NBA.com|date=September 15, 2020|access-date=September 15, 2020}}</ref>

On February 28, 2021, Washington scored a then career-high 42 points to help the [[Charlotte Hornets]] win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|title=P.J. Washington scores career-high 42 points.|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/video/2021/03/01/20210301-p-j-washington-scores-career-high-42-points#:~:text=Washington%20scores%20career%2Dhigh%2042%20points,-P.J.%20Washington%20scores|website=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2021|access-date=March 1, 2021}}</ref> On March 28, 2023, he scored a career-high 43 points in a 137–134 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Perley|title=Hornets Win Wild One In OKC Behind Washington's Career-High 43 PTS|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-win-wild-one-in-okc-behind-washingtons-career-high-43-pts|website=NBA.com|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=March 28, 2023}}</ref> On August 29, Washington re-signed with the Hornets on a 3-year, $48 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Re-Sign P.J. Washington Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-re-sign-p-j-washington-jr|website=NBA.com|date=August 29, 2023|access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|title=P.J. Washington staying with Hornets on new 3-year, $48M deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/38264436/pj-washington-staying-hornets-new-3-year-48m-deal|website=ESPN.com|date=August 26, 2023|access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> On January 27, 2024, Washington tied his career-high 43 points in a 134–122 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Markkanen scores 33, Jazz build 36-point lead in 134–122 victory over Hornets|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585275|website=ESPN.com|date=January 27, 2024|access-date=January 29, 2024}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2024–present)===
On February 8, 2024, Washington was traded, alongside two future second–round picks, to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Seth Curry]], [[Grant Williams (basketball)|Grant Williams]], and a 2027 first–round pick that is top 2 protected.<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=MAVERICKS ACQUIRE WASHINGTON, GAFFORD TO BOLSTER FRONT LINE|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-trades/|website=Mavs.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref> On February 10, Washington made his Mavericks debut, putting up 14 points, five rebounds, and one steal in a 146–111 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/mavericks-dallas-takeaways-pj-washington-jr-daniel-gafford-win-thunder|title=3 Mavericks takeaways after PJ Washington Jr, Daniel Gafford debut in win vs. Thunder|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mistretta|first=Joey|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=February 10, 2024}}</ref> On April 5, Washington put up 32 points alongside a game-winner in a 108–106 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/mavericks-news-pj-washington-clutch-warriors-luka-doncic-absence|title=Mavericks' PJ Washington goes full clutch-mode vs. Warriors amid Luka Doncic's absence|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mistretta|first=Joey|date=April 5, 2024|access-date=April 5, 2024}}</ref> On April 26, in Game 3 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs#(4) Los Angeles Clippers vs. (5) Dallas Mavericks|first round of the playoffs]] against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] during a 101–90 win, Washington was ejected after being involved in a confrontation with [[Russell Westbrook]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ward-Henninger |first=Colin |date=April 26, 2024 |title=Russell Westbrook, PJ Washington ejected from Game 3 after hard foul on Luka Doncic |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/mavericks-clippers-russell-westbrook-pj-washington-ejected-from-game-3-after-hard-foul-on-luka-doncic/ |access-date=April 27, 2024 |work=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> On May 11, in Game 3 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs#(1) Oklahoma City Thunder vs. (5) Dallas Mavericks|Western Conference Semifinals]], Washington led the Mavericks with 27 points during a 105–101 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/thunder-mavericks-5-takeaways-game-3-2024-nba-playoffs|title=Thunder-Mavericks: 5 takeaways as P.J. Washington comes through in Game 3|website=nba.com|last=Wright|first=Michael|date=May 11, 2024|access-date=May 11, 2024}}</ref> In Game 6, Washington was fouled on a three-point attempt by [[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]] with 2.5 seconds to go. He sunk the first two free throws to put the Mavericks up by 1 and intentionally missed the third. [[Jalen Williams]] subsequently missed a half court shot, and the Mavericks beat the Thunder in a 117–116 victory to advance to the Western Conference Finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/thunder-mavericks-recap-game-6-2024-west-semifinals|title=P.J. Washington's free throws finish rally as Mavs beat Thunder 117–116 to reach West finals|website=nba.com|last=Dixon|first=Schuyler|date=May 18, 2024|access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> Washington helped the Mavericks reach the [[2024 NBA Finals]] where they lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|publisher=cbsnews.com|access-date=June 17, 2024|date=June 17, 2024}}</ref>

On December 27, 2024, Washington was involved in an altercation with [[Jusuf Nurkić]].<ref>{{cite web | title=NBA announces penalties from Mavericks-Suns game | website=NBA Communications | date=December 28, 2024 | url=https://pr.nba.com/mavericks-suns-suspensions/ | access-date=December 1, 2025}}</ref> The next day, Washington was suspended for a game due to the altercation.

On September 10, 2025, Washington signed a four-year, $88.76 million extension with the Mavericks that runs through the 2029–30 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mavericks F P.J. Washington agrees to 4-year, $90M extension|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46146191/mavericks-f-pj-washington-agrees-4-year-90m-extension|publisher=espn.com|access-date=September 21, 2025|date=September 3, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Washington's parents met at [[Middle Tennessee State University|Middle Tennessee State]], where they both played basketball. Upon graduation, his father became a General Manager at a car sales company and coached his middle school team, while his mother went on to become a teacher at his middle school. Washington has a brother, Spencer, and a sister, Alexandria.<ref name=":0" />

Washington married Alisah Chanel in October 2023, with whom he has a son, named Preston.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Macasero |first=Michael |date=October 30, 2023 |title=PJ Washington ties the knot with his second baby mama Alisah Chanel 2 years after breaking up with Brittany Renner |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/news-pj-washington-ties-knot-second-baby-mama-alisah-chanel-2-years-breaking-brittany-renner |website=Sportskeeda}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=THE WASHINGTONS 💍 Part 1 🤍 |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Cy948WDMTRr/?utm_source=ig_embed&img_index=1 |access-date=May 13, 2024 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> He also has a son named Paul Jamaine Washington III, born in 2021 with Brittany Renner.<ref>{{Cite web |last=staff |first=B. C.
